chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Harun, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, who through his chain linked it up to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him),

he passed by the butchers and forbade them from selling seven things from the sheep: he forbade them from selling the blood, the glands, the corners of the heart, the spleen, the marrow, the testicles, and the penis. A man from the butchers said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, the liver and the spleen are the same.' He said to him: 'You are lying, O Liar! Bring me two bowls of water, and I will show you the difference between them.' He was brought a liver, a spleen, and two bowls of water. He said: 'Squeeze each one of them in a separate vessel, and squeeze them both together as commanded.' The liver contracted and nothing came out of it, but the spleen did not contract, and all that was inside it came out, and it was all blood, and its skin and veins remained. He said: 'This is the difference between them; this is meat, and this is blood.'
ai.seo_question: What are the seven forbidden parts of the sheep in Shia jurisprudence and how did Imam Ali distinguish the liver from the spleen?
ai.summary: In this famous narrative from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) refutes the butcher's claim that the liver and spleen are identical by demonstrating their distinct physical natures: the liver is solid meat (lawn), while the spleen is primarily blood (dam). This empirical distinction underpins the jurisprudential ruling that the liver is permissible to eat, whereas the spleen, being a repository of blood, is forbidden, illustrating the Shia scholarly emphasis on linking textual rulings to observable physical realities.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-4 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Harun, on the authority of Abi Yahya al-Vaseti who through a chain of narrations linked it up to the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB)

who went to the butchers and admonished them against selling seven parts of sheep: The blood; the glands; the corners of the heart; the spleens; the bone marrow; the balls and the penis.” One of the butchers told him (MGB), ‘O Commander of the Faithful! The spleens and the liver are the same.’The Commander of the Faithful (MGB) told him, ‘O liar! You are lying! Bring me two bowls of water so that I may show you the difference between them.’ He brought two bowls of water. The Commander of the Faithful (MGB) took a liver and a spleen and put each one in one of the bowls of water. He (MGB) then squashed each one of them with his hand. The liver got squashed but no blood came out of it, but the spleen did not. There was a lot of blood in it which all came out into the water, and all that was left of it was the veins and the skin that was in it. Then the Commander of the Faithful (MGB) said, ‘This is the difference between the liver and the spleens. The first one is a form of meat, but the second one is just blood!’”
